Godson-Afful asks over decline in discipline Source : Kareen Tei 20 November 2026 6:24pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Head Pastor of Rehoboth Network of Churches, Rev. Dr Henry Godson-Afful, has questioned what disciplinary measures have replaced corporal punishment in Ghanaian schools, warning that the absence of effective alternatives could undermine discipline among pupils.
He said although removing the cane from classrooms was understandable, the decision should have been accompanied by alternative approaches to correcting inappropriate behaviour and instilling discipline.
Speaking on JoyNews' AM Show on Friday, November 20, to mark World Children's Day, Rev. Godson-Afful said the country needed to reconsider how schools maintained discipline while protecting children's rights.
"One of the reasons why discipline has gone down the drain is that we took the cane out of the classroom, which, fair enough, but what did we replace it with?" he asked.
He argued that the focus should now be on identifying effective disciplinary measures that would encourage responsible behaviour and keep pupils committed to their education.
"The alternative, I think, is what we need to, on a day like this, start thinking through. What have we replaced the cane with? What are the alternative disciplinary measures that will help the child stay in the curriculum?" he said.
Rev. Godson-Afful called on parents, teachers, policymakers and other stakeholders to engage in discussions on appropriate ways to correct children without compromising their welfare and educational development.
His comments come amid ongoing discussions about how schools can balance children's rights and protection with the need to maintain order and promote responsible behaviour in the classroom.
This year's World Children's Day is being celebrated under the theme, "My Day, My Rights, My Future", which highlights the importance of creating safe and supportive environments for children to thrive.
